analysis:
The only change in this PR is a one-line documentation edit in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 52, hunk @@ -49,7 +49,7 @@). It rewords the GLM video-input description: the old text named inline `data:video/mp4` / `data:video/quicktime` URLs, and the new text says 'inline base64 MP4 or QuickTime URL, constant or variable frame rate; labels in MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders' and keeps '2 FPS, decoded target-only'. No code, configuration, key handling, authorization, attestation or encryption path changes. The base unit (lines 1672-1821) is unchanged context covering env-var passthrough, prefix-cache defaults (T-041), the App Attest worker flag and runtime constants. I found nothing there that this PR alters.

Threat relevance: the edit touches the media ingest surface (T-050, inline video plaintext via temp files). It is documentation only, so it cannot regress the control. The reference to MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders and variable-frame-rate support suggests a companion source change that is not in this batch. That change could widen the accepted container/label set and alter decoding, temp-file or resource-exhaustion exposure. It should be reviewed where that source diff appears, specifically that video plaintext stays out of FileManager temp files (T-050) and that decoded size and frame count are bounded. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.

No threat-model update is needed from the doc edit alone. No secrets are exposed. Nothing in the text weakens a stated security property; it does not claim new secrecy or correctness guarantees (T-056).
